subject: Log sunset window & provenance statement for SOC 2
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@serenitybio.com>

Date: 2026-05-26T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Log sunset window & provenance statement for SOC 2

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our SOC 2 auditor has a couple of specific asks around Redwood's log lifecycle for tenant-scoped debug/session traces and how you can demonstrate deletion happened (they call this a provenance statement). Two concrete questions: 

1) What is Redwood's standard retention window for transient/session/debug logs tied to a tenant? We currently have a 30-day expectation documented, but the auditor wants explicit confirmation.

2) For customers that require longer holds, can Redwood apply a tenant-specific sunset window (e.g., 90 days) and if so what controls or compensating measures are available (encryption-at-rest, restricted access, audit logs for deletion events)?

For the SOC 2 review we need a short provenance statement we can include in the evidence set that explains the deletion process end-to-end (who/what triggers deletion, what artifacts are created to prove deletion, where deletion events are logged, and retention-of-proof). If you can also share a sanitized sample of a deletion audit (CSV or log excerpt) and a short runbook or pointer to the CAIQ/SIG mapping that covers log disposition, that would help accelerate sign-off.

Can you let us know next steps and an estimated ETA? We are aiming to get the auditor everything by 6/2.

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Sr. Security Program Manager
Serenity Bio

Attachments: none

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Looping in Marissa (security/compliance) and Karthik (platform engineering) so we can collate the artifacts. High-level answers up front:

- Default tenant-scoped debug/session logs: 30 days configurable.
- Tenant-specific extensions: yes — we support per-tenant retention policies up to 365 days for hosted customers via a policy flag; for dedicated/private deployments we can align to contract.

Deliverables we can produce for your auditor by 6/2:
1) A one-page provenance statement describing the deletion flow (who/what/when).
2) A sanitized sample deletion audit (CSV) showing deletion event records, timestamps, and operator/service IDs.
3) The deletion runbook (PDF stub) describing the API calls and background job flow.
4) A mapping doc pointer for CAIQ/SIG sections that reference log disposition (we will highlight relevant sections).

Karthik — can you confirm the exact API field names we should call out (retention_days, tenant_policy_id) and whether we can produce an export of deletion events for the last 90 days as sample?

Alice — small caveat: for extended retention (>=90 days) we recommend enabling restricted-access mode + encryption key rotation policies as compensating controls; we will call these out in the provenance statement so your auditor sees controls in place.

I attached the provisional filenames we plan to deliver; will post links as soon as Karthik confirms the export. ETA: initial artifacts by EOD 5/27, finalized package by 6/1.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Principal, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

On Wed, 2026-05-26 at 17:04, Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Naomi: Karthik — can you confirm the exact API field names we should call out (retention_days, tenant_policy_id) and whether we can produce an export of deletion events for the last 90 days as sample?

Thanks Naomi — quick technical details below so the provenance statement can be explicit for the auditor.

Deletion flow (summary):
- Trigger: tenant policy expiration or explicit tenant API call (DELETE /v1/tenants/{id}/logs or PATCH /v1/tenants/{id} {"retention_days":45}).
- Execution: background worker picks up a deletion job, removes per-tenant log objects from live stores, purges KV-cache entries, and enqueues a deletion-confirmation event to the audit stream.
- Proof artifacts: audit stream entries include event_id, timestamp, actor (service:log-cleaner or user:ops), tenant_id, object_count, sha256_of_manifest; successful deletion emits a signed confirmation token persisted to the audit index.
- Backups: snapshots are on a 7-day rolling backup for hosted; we zero-out / mark deleted entries in backups according to our backup-retention policy and capture deletion metadata. For customers requiring proof of final erasure from backups we offer a backup-sunset coordination and attestation under separate contract terms.

API field names to include: "retention_days", "tenant_policy_id", "deletion_job_id".

Sample export: we can produce a sanitized CSV of deletion events covering the last 90 days (redacted tenant ids -> tenant-XXX) and include the signed confirmation token hashes. See planned attachment: deletion-audit-sample.csv.

Compensating controls for extended holds (>=90 days):
- Encryption-at-rest (customer-managed KMS recommended)
- Restricted-access role (read-only access for a small ops group)
- Enhanced audit retention of deletion-proof tokens for the hold window

I will upload the sample CSV and runbook to the security drive and share a link by EOD.

—Karthik
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: deletion-audit-sample.csv (sanitized), redwood-deletion-runbook.pdf

1) Procurement needs a one-paragraph statement we can paste into contract exhibits that says: "Redwood will maintain tenant-scoped debug/session logs for N days and will provide deletion provenance upon request" with the placeholder N replaced depending on the negotiated term. Can you provide that exact wording plus a short clause on how deletion-proofing is retained?

2) Auditor follow-up: can you explicitly state how deletion from backups is handled for hosted customers vs dedicated/private deployments? Karthik's note is useful but the auditor wants concrete contract-eligible language (we may include a separate backup sundown schedule if needed).

3) Please attach the sanitized CSV and the provenance statement text file in your reply so our security team can upload to the auditor portal. We will treat the CSV as confidential.

If you can send the three items (one-paragraph contract text, deletion-provenance-statement.txt, and deletion-audit-sample.csv) as attachments by EOD 5/28 we can close this item for the SOC 2 pack.

Best,
Alice
